## Active Learning {.unnumbered}

Class time is for working on problems, not only for listening.
You will be asked to think about questions on your own, write down answers,
discuss them in small groups, and share your answers with the class.
Sometimes you may be asked to write on the board.
I will give you time to think things through before you are put on the spot.
Please give me feedback about the structure of the class, the activities, or group dynamics.

### ABCD Cards {.unnumbered}

On the first day of class, I will give each student an ABCD card,
which you will use to vote on answers to questions in class.
They work like electronic clickers, but they are free and need no batteries.
They let both you and me quickly see how well you understand the material,
so that I can adjust what I emphasize in class
and you can adjust what you study outside it.
Please bring this card to class each day.
If you lose your card,
print a new, landscape-mode color copy of the [ABCD card](../images/abcd-card.pdf).

### Worksheets {.unnumbered}

Most classes include a worksheet:
guided practice that reinforces the day's concepts and prepares you for the exams.
Please keep your worksheets organized and bring them to later classes.
You are encouraged to work on worksheet problems with classmates,
but each student submits their own work and should be able to explain it.
I will post selected worksheet solutions after the submission deadline,
and review common mistakes at the start of the next class.
Most midterm and final exam questions will be adapted from worksheet problems.
